entries.title: Ama and the Lost Little Goat
entries.summary: Ama’s little goat Pepe goes missing. She asks her neighbours, listens carefully, and finds him.

entries.title: Kofi’s Colourful Garden
entries.summary: Kofi plants seeds, waits patiently and discovers a garden full of colours, with counting along the way.

entries.title: The Clever Tortoise and the Rain
entries.summary: In a long dry season, a tortoise who watches carefully works out that rain is coming and gets everyone working together.

entries.title: Amina’s First Day at School
entries.summary: Amina is nervous on her first day at school, but a kind teacher and a new friend help her feel brave.

entries.title: The Little Star That Loved to Shine
entries.summary: A very small star thinks she is too tiny to matter, until her light guides a traveller home.

entries.title: Efua’s Honest Business
entries.summary: Efua starts a small after-school business selling groundnut cakes and must decide how far to go to win more customers.

entries.title: Yaa and the Blocked Drain
entries.summary: After heavy rain floods the lane outside her home, Yaa investigates why the water will not drain and leads her neighbours in clearing the drain and keeping it clear.

entries.title: Kofi Counts the Market
entries.summary: Kofi helps Mama at the market and counts everything he sees, from one tomato to ten oranges, until he counts the best thing of all.

entries.title: Abena and the Beginning of Everything
entries.summary: Visiting the Ghana Radio Astronomy Observatory at Kuntunse, Abena explores how space itself expands, what evidence supports the Big Bang, and which cosmic questions scientists are still working to answer.

entries.title: Kojo and the Forest of a Thousand Lives
entries.summary: Walking through Kakum National Park with his aunt, Ranger Akosua, Kojo discovers how giant trees, cocoa midges, fruit bats, monkeys and tiny decomposers depend on one another in a living food web.

entries.title: Yaa and the Mystery of Changing Life
entries.summary: At a natural history exhibition in Accra, Yaa and Kwame investigate fossils, beetle camouflage and family trees to understand how populations evolve by natural selection over generations.

entries.title: Adwoa and the Missing Market Change
entries.summary: Sent to the market with a twenty-cedi note, Adwoa uses careful mental addition and subtraction to spot an extra four cedis in her change and chooses to return it honestly.

entries.title: Kwaku’s Little Savings Box
entries.summary: With a small wooden susu box built from his father’s carpentry offcuts, ten-year-old Kwaku learns to separate needs from wants, budget his weekly five cedis, and help his family and himself.

entries.title: Kwame and the Talking Drum
entries.summary: Six-year-old Kwame learns from his grandfather Nana Yaw that before you can play the Akan atumpan talking drums, or any of Ghana’s diverse drums, you must first listen with your ears and your heart.

entries.title: The Secret Beneath Lake Bosomtwe
entries.summary: Visiting Lake Bosomtwe in the Ashanti Region, Kwabena and his cousin Afia hear both the respected traditional oral history of the sacred lake and the geological evidence showing how a meteorite impact formed the crater over a million years ago.

entries.title: The Ocean That Hides a Thousand Secrets
entries.summary: At a marine science laboratory in Tema, thirteen-year-old Tetteh and his classmate Ama explore deep-sea footage from the Atlantic Ocean, discovering how ocean zones, crushing pressure, bioluminescence and hydrothermal vents support life without sunlight.

entries.title: Esi and the Elephant’s Secret Path
entries.summary: Near Mole National Park in northern Ghana, eight-year-old Esi learns from Ranger Braimah how elephant families follow their wise grandmother along ancient paths, talk through the ground with low rumbles, and stay safe around farms with beehive fences.

entries.title: Kofi and the Invisible Giant
entries.summary: At the Ghana Planetarium in Accra, fourteen-year-old Kofi investigates how black holes form, why they are not cosmic vacuum cleaners, what happens at the event horizon, how astronomers detect invisible giants, and which mysteries of quantum gravity remain unsolved.

entries.title: The Tree That Saved Our Playground
entries.summary: When the sunny side of their school playground becomes too hot at break time, seven-year-old Kwame and his classmates discover how their big neem tree cools the air and work together to plant and care for new shade trees.

entries.title: Akosua and the Rainfall Puzzle
entries.summary: When her classmates argue about which day of the week had the heaviest rain in Koforidua, ten-year-old Akosua builds a proper rain gauge with her science teacher, records five days of millimetre data in a bar graph, and learns the difference between daily weather and long-term climate.

entries.title: Ama’s Journey Above the Rainforest
entries.summary: Nine-year-old Ama welcomes her cousin Jayden from London to Kakum National Park in the Central Region, where their walk across the high canopy bridges reveals how responsible ecotourism protects Ghana’s rainforests, wildlife and fresh water.

entries.title: The Courage of Yaa Asantewaa
entries.summary: On a school visit to the Manhyia Palace Museum in Kumasi, eleven-year-old Kwaku and his sister Abena explore the verified history of Nana Yaa Asantewaa, the sacred Golden Stool, and the 1900 resistance against British colonial rule, learning how historians use evidence.

entries.title: Kojo’s Amazing Greenhouse Farm
entries.summary: When heavy rains and whiteflies damage his uncle’s open tomato field on the Accra Plains, eleven-year-old Kojo investigates how a tropical greenhouse manages light, heat, ventilation, drip irrigation, pests and farm budgets, and how a farm greenhouse differs from Earth’s atmospheric greenhouse effect.

entries.title: Akosua’s Prayer and the Unfinished Homework
entries.summary: Ten-year-old Akosua believes deeply in God as Supreme and prays earnestly for exam success, yet leaves her mathematics and science workbook unfinished. Her grandmother Nana Esi lovingly helps her see how genuine faith inspires diligence, preparation, humility and service to others.

entries.title: Efua and the Business That Almost Failed
entries.summary: In this sequel to Efua’s Honest Business, thirteen-year-old Efua sells a record one hundred packs of groundnut cakes in a single week, yet her cash tin runs short when she goes to restock! With Nana Ama and Auntie Dede, she learns to separate revenue, fixed and variable costs, profit, and cash flow.

entries.title: The Door That Remembered
entries.summary: On an educational visit to Cape Coast Castle, JHS students Kojo and Esi walk with a Ghana Museums and Monuments Board educator and visitors from the African diaspora, learning why preserving the history of the transatlantic slave trade teaches human dignity, justice and our responsibility to future generations.

entries.title: From Kumasi to the World: The Girl Who Built a Billion-Dollar Idea
entries.summary: In a fictional journey spanning from a JHS science club in Kumasi to a pan-African engineering enterprise, Serwaa develops a low-cost solar-powered cold-storage system to prevent post-harvest farm losses, discovering how prototypes, setbacks, equity investors and company valuation work in the real world.

entries.title: Kofi’s One-Cedi Business
entries.summary: Eight-year-old Kofi starts with a single one-cedi coin and a big question: can you really start a business with one cedi? With help from his sister Ama and cousin Yaw, he learns how pooling small capital, solving a real customer problem, and subtracting cost from revenue create honest profit.

entries.title: Abena Buys a Piece of a Company
entries.summary: Thirteen-year-old Abena visits her Auntie Esi in Accra and discovers how the Ghana Stock Exchange (GSE), regulated by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC Ghana), allows ordinary citizens to buy shares of companies or lend money through bonds, and why diversification, patience and avoiding "get-rich-quick" scams protect long-term wealth.

entries.title: The Umbrella Before the Rain
entries.summary: When a sudden midnight storm blows the roof off a neighbour’s provision store while Auntie Akosua’s insured tailoring shop recovers quickly, eleven-year-old Yaw learns how insurance, risk pooling, premiums, claims, deductibles, NHIS health protection and the National Insurance Commission (NIC) protect families from sudden financial shocks.

entries.title: Grandpa Mensah’s Secret to a Peaceful Retirement
entries.summary: Twelve-year-old Efua and her brother Kojo wonder how retired headmaster Grandpa Mensah and retired market trader Grandma Mansa still receive dependable monthly income without working every day, discovering how pensions, compound growth, inflation protection and Ghana’s Three-Tier Pension System (SSNIT, Tier 2 and Tier 3 under NPRA) turn decades of steady contributions into a peaceful retirement.

entries.title: The App That Created a Hundred Jobs
entries.summary: In a fictional multi-year story beginning at a JHS coding club in Accra, Kwame and Adwoa learn why building an app without talking to users fails, and how customer discovery, low-bandwidth engineering, data privacy under Ghana’s Data Protection Act (Act 843), fair commission splits and years of perseverance grow a trusted repair-services platform that supports a hundred decent jobs.

entries.title: The Promise That Bought a Vote
entries.summary: During a fictional local council election in the town of Asasekro, fourteen-year-old Kofi and his classmate Ama notice one candidate handing out gifts and making huge uncosted promises while another shares a written budget plan, prompting the students to investigate how public budgets, independent verification, secret ballots and civic accountability really work.

entries.title: The River That Lost Its Voice
entries.summary: Twelve-year-old Esi and her grandfather Nana Kwaku notice that the once-clear Subri stream near their farming town has turned thick and yellowish-brown from destructive illegal mining upstream, leading Esi’s class and certified environmental scientists to investigate sediment, water treatment, laboratory testing for heavy metals, and lawful, sustainable livelihoods.

entries.title: The Journey That Almost Took Everything
entries.summary: Twenty-year-old Kwabena, frustrated after months of searching for steady work, is tempted by a flashy social-media agent promising an instant job abroad through an unverified overland route for 35,000 cedis, until his JHS sister Afia, his cousin Uncle Tetteh who returned from an unsafe journey, and a nurse cousin working legally abroad help him separate dangerous fraud from legal migration and real technical careers in Ghana.

entries.title: Adwoa Refused to Be Limited
entries.summary: Eleven-year-old Adwoa loves gears, levers and building things, even when a neighbour claims engineering is only for boys. Encouraged by her parents, who share cooking, budgeting and workshop duties equally at home, her brother Kojo, and mechanical engineer Auntie Serwaa, Adwoa designs a pedal-powered groundnut sheller that shells thirty kilograms an hour instead of five.

entries.title: The Town Where Everybody Waited
entries.summary: In a busy neighbourhood where everyone complains about litter and blocked roadside drains while waiting for "somebody else" to act, ten-year-old Yao and nine-year-old Akosua team up with their teacher Mr Mensah for a safe, adult-supervised school recycling drive and a community petition that brings the District Assembly sanitation crew and neighbours together.

entries.title: We Built It Here in Ghana
entries.summary: Following a fictional multi-year journey from an agricultural club in Sunyani to a certified agro-processing enterprise, cousin founders Mensah and Mansa turn surplus ripe plantains and cassava into shelf-stable snacks and flour, overcoming equipment breakdowns, high loan rates, and strict FDA Ghana and GSA quality standards to build a sustainable business supporting 18 factory staff and 45 smallholder farmers.

entries.title: The Dream That Powered a Nation
entries.summary: On a fictional school excursion to the Akosombo Dam in the Eastern Region, twelve-year-old Sena and her classmate Kwaku learn how the historic Volta River Project converts falling water into electricity, while also discovering the real human displacement, environmental changes and ethical responsibilities that come with nation-building infrastructure.

entries.title: The Girl Who Taught a Drone to See
entries.summary: Fourteen-year-old Mansa and her school coding club build an artificial-intelligence camera system to help maize farmers spot crop disease early, only to see their first model fail in real Ghanaian farm conditions until they learn about training-data bias, farmer privacy, field testing and human agricultural expertise.

entries.title: The Cocoa Bean That Travelled the World
entries.summary: Ten-year-old Adwoa follows cocoa pods from her family’s shaded farm in the Western North Region to a Ghanaian cocoa-processing and chocolate factory in Tema, discovering how fermentation, quality grading, roasting, manufacturing, packaging and branding add value along the global supply chain.

entries.title: The Butterfly That Knew the Way
entries.summary: During a school nature-club session near Aburi, eight-year-old Nhyira notices a swallowtail butterfly with a tiny chipped wing returning to the exact same hibiscus bush two mornings in a row, leading her class to discover how insects see ultraviolet flower guides, smell with their antennae, taste with their feet, and navigate their habitats.

entries.title: The Money That Worked While Afia Slept
entries.summary: When twelve-year-old Afia helps her older brother Yao decide what to do with 1,000 cedis earned from his carpentry apprentice work, their aunt at a licensed community bank teaches them how compound interest, inflation, investment risk, debt compounding and get-rich-quick Ponzi scams work.

entries.title: The Village That Refused to Give Up
entries.summary: When the dry season shrinks the seasonal stream in the fictional village of Nsuom and the old hand-pump breaks down, eleven-year-old Kwame and his neighbours learn how faith in God inspires unity, scientific hydrogeology, laboratory water-quality testing, transparent budgeting and shared maintenance rather than passive waiting.

entries.title: The Sea That Came Closer
entries.summary: When eleven-year-old Teye and his friend Akweley find that the sea has reached their beach football field, Grandpa Nii, Madam Ofori and a visiting coastal scientist help them investigate coastal erosion, test how waves move sediment, reject polluting shortcuts, and present evidence-based solutions at a community meeting.

entries.title: The Queen of the Market
entries.summary: Nine-year-old Adom visits a busy Kumasi market with Grandma Akua and meets Auntie Serwaa, a respected trader who solves disputes fairly, keeps honest records, refuses to mix spoiled tomatoes with fresh ones, and inspires Adom’s class to create record books and celebrate the women who help build Ghana’s economy.

entries.title: The Mosquito Detective
entries.summary: When Nana Yaw blames mosquitoes for every fever in Ghana, his sister Abena and their teacher Madam Lamptey turn the class into science detectives, learning that Plasmodium parasites transmitted by infected female Anopheles mosquitoes cause malaria, why standing water and treated bed nets matter, and why fevers require professional medical testing rather than guessing.

entries.title: The Village That Owned a Factory
entries.summary: Near Nsawam, fourteen-year-old Naa and her friend Sadiq ask whether local pineapple farmers could reduce post-harvest losses by forming an adult-run processing cooperative, learning about member ownership, feasibility budgets, capital gaps, shares versus bonds, honest financial reporting and job creation.

entries.title: The Boy Who Built a Voice
entries.summary: When fifteen-year-old Elorm joins the robotics club using a tablet and gestures to communicate, he and Kobby co-design an assistive text-to-speech app that handles Ghanaian names accurately, respects voice privacy and consent, includes offline backup boards, and proves that the best inventions begin by listening to users.

entries.title: The Night the Stars Asked Questions
entries.summary: When an evening power cut plunges twelve-year-old Araba’s courtyard into darkness, Grandma Esi and her science teacher guide her through the wonders of distant starlight, exoplanets, dark matter, binary-star planets, evaluating sensational alien headlines, and the excitement of unanswered scientific questions.

entries.title: Selasi and the Five Drums
entries.summary: Selasi counts five drums in the yard, watches them disappear into friends’ hands, and finds her own clever way to join the music.

entries.title: Dede and the Puddle
entries.summary: After the rain, Dede splashes in a big puddle, meets a butterfly, and wonders where her puddle goes when the sun comes out.

entries.title: Ananse and the Noisy Pot
entries.summary: Ananse tries to carry a pot of groundnut soup into the forest to eat alone, but the noisy lid gives him away, and a small antelope has a kinder idea.

entries.title: Little Hen’s Big Sneeze
entries.summary: Little Hen’s big sneeze makes Goat, Dog and Duck jump, bark and flap, until a tiny chick works out what is tickling her nose.

entries.title: Goodnight, Little Compound
entries.summary: A rhyming bedtime poem that says goodnight to the goats, the mango tree, the drum and the family, one sleepy couplet at a time.

entries.title: Zainab’s Big Feelings
entries.summary: When her balloon pops at a party, Zainab feels sad and cross at the same time, and uses her grandmother’s breathing trick to feel calmer.

entries.title: Ananse and the Pot of Wisdom
entries.summary: Ananse tries to keep all the wisdom in the world in one pot, until his young son Ntikuma shows him a better way to climb, and wisdom is shared with everyone.

entries.title: Two Ways to Say Thank You
entries.summary: In a busy Accra classroom, Akua and her new friend Sefakor swap thank-you words in Twi and Ewe, and the class builds a wall of thanks in every language they know.

entries.title: The Slowest Drummer
entries.summary: Kweku learns rhythms more slowly than everyone else in the school drum club, but at the school concert his steady beat is what saves the performance.

entries.title: Fiifi Goes Back for His Book
entries.summary: Fiifi realises on the way to school that he has left his reading book at home, remembers a Sankofa saying from his grandmother, and decides to go back.

entries.title: The Tomato Detectives
entries.summary: Ewurama and Issah turn a market-stall problem into a fair test: do tomatoes spoil faster in the sun or in the shade? They repeat their test, report honestly, and plan the next question.

entries.title: Delali’s Rain Gauge
entries.summary: Delali builds a rain gauge from a plastic bottle to prove to her grandfather whether the rains are late. When her classmate’s gauge disagrees, they investigate why, and learn what a small set of data can and cannot tell you.

entries.title: More Than a Medal
entries.summary: Nuhu never wins on Sports Day, so his friend Ewoenam helps him measure something else: how much faster he gets. Together they ask for a ribbon that celebrates improvement as well as winning.

entries.title: The Voice Note
entries.summary: A forwarded voice note claims tomorrow’s school is closed. Lamiokor and her classmates check where it came from before passing it on, and make a poster for their noticeboard on how to do it.

entries.title: The Phone Case Plan
entries.summary: Mawunyo and Bright run a small supervised school project to sell phone cases, learning to count the real costs, price fairly, answer customers honestly and measure success in more than cedis.

entries.title: The Freezer That Keeps Tomorrow
entries.summary: A science club asks what happens if the last pangolin disappears. They discover frozen zoos, test what freezing does to living cells with a tomato, and learn why a freezer can buy time but cannot replace a forest.

entries.title: The Missing Label
entries.summary: On a school trip to the Aburi Botanical Gardens, Etse and Pearl find a tree with no readable label and become plant detectives, learning why gardens exist, why one plant can have many names, and how knowledge should be shared with respect.

entries.title: Seeds That Wait in the Cold
entries.summary: When her grandmother’s favourite garden egg disappears from the market, Mavis tests how old seeds lose their power to sprout and discovers how Ghana’s national gene bank and a far-away vault in Norway guard seeds for the future.

entries.title: Faces That Look Like Ours
entries.summary: Two friends in a school library follow fossils from Morocco to a cave in Ghana, build a timeline on the field, learn how alike all people are, and write down what scientists still do not know about the story of our species.

entries.title: The Dinosaur in the Yard
entries.summary: A cousin claims that a hen is a kind of dinosaur. To test the idea, Abeiku and Naomi stretch a rope across the school field where one metre equals a million years, and discover how long ago dinosaurs lived, what happened to them, where in Africa their bones have been found, and why birds are still around.

entries.title: The Lake That Fell From the Sky
entries.summary: Edem and Afrakoma stand on the rim of Lake Bosumtwi and ask why it is so round. They test three explanations against the evidence, learn how glass beads in Côte d’Ivoire point back to Ghana, and finish with a list of what is known and still unknown.

entries.title: Little Turtle’s Big Swim
entries.summary: A tiny turtle hatches on a dark Ghanaian beach and crawls towards the shining sea, while a little girl helps by keeping the lights off.

entries.title: The Backyard Safari
entries.summary: Dela turns her yard into a safari with tube binoculars and a notebook, and discovers that insects have six legs, spiders have eight, and a very small adventure can be full of surprises.

entries.title: The Treasure Under the Mango Tree
entries.summary: Grandfather’s hand-drawn map says “ten steps north, five steps east”, but the children’s steps are shorter than his. Yayra and Kojovi measure, calculate, and find the treasure together.

entries.title: Lost in the Green Cathedral
entries.summary: On a school visit to a rainforest reserve, Selina and Ebo stray from the path and realise they are lost. Instead of running, they stop, think, make themselves easy to find, and stay calm until help arrives.

entries.title: The Ghosts of Old Akokoaso
entries.summary: Children say that the abandoned old village is haunted. Yakubu and Adoma ask the elders for permission and study the “ghosts” like detectives, learning why the village was left and why its story matters.

entries.title: Down Where the Light Ends
entries.summary: Aba flies a robot submarine down through the sunlight, twilight and midnight zones of the Gulf of Guinea. When the cable snags, she must stay calm and think before she acts, and then she records a creature nobody can name.

entries.title: Ninety-Two Minutes
entries.summary: In a fictional future, four Ghanaian student cadets are left alone on a small orbital station after a power fault and a delayed shuttle. They count their water, oxygen and food, plan for the worst, share the work and send a message home, every ninety-two minutes.
